title: HPA/KEDA metric drift causing premature scale-downs during bursty workloads - investigation and actions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a weekend spike in traffic for several hosted workloads we observed repeated premature scale-downs followed by rapid scale-ups (scale thrash) that increased request latency and bumped token cost by ~18% for affected customers. This ticket captures the investigation into HPA and KEDA metric selection, smoothing parameters, and cold-start interactions plus recommended fixes and follow-ups.
incident_summary: At 2025-10-31 22:07 UTC an upstream traffic burst hit multiple API routes. HPA+KEDA combined scaling decisions led to scale-downs within 30-60s after short lulls caused by request batching. Subsequent rehydration of pods (cold-start) caused 2-3x latency spikes and at times request errors due to readiness gating. Alerts triggered for elevated 95th latency and pod churn; autoscaler alerts fired for rapid replica changes.
timeline: 2025-10-31 22:07 UTC - Spike begins; 22:09 UTC - KEDA scaler triggers scale-up for queue-length-based scaler; 22:10-22:20 - HPA scales down because CPU and pod-based custom metrics dip below threshold; 22:22 UTC - Prometheus smoothing window reports delayed queue growth because of metric scrape frequency; 22:23 UTC - Pod readiness delays cause failed in-flight requests; 22:30 UTC - Traffic reduces, replication stabilizes; 23:00 UTC - SRE begins investigation; 2025-11-01 09:00 UTC - Initial mitigation applied (increase HPA scale-down stabilization-window); 2025-11-02 - Full postmortem investigation starts.
observations: 1) Metric mismatch: KEDA uses queue-length at 5s granularity, HPA uses aggregated CPU util (30s) and a custom rolling-window request-per-second metric (60s). These differing windows allowed transient dips to be interpreted as sustained low load by HPA.
root_cause: Primary: Inconsistent metric windows and thresholds between KEDA scalers and HPA causing conflicting signals. Secondary: aggressive HPA scale-down configuration (stabilizationWindowSeconds=30, tolerance=0.1) with no warm-pool or pre-warm behavior; cold-start latency for model-serving containers is significant (startup + model load ~6-10s) leading to user-visible latency during scale-ups.
mitigations_taken: Short-term: Increased HPA scale-down stabilizationWindowSeconds to 300s for affected deployments; bumped target CPU tolerance to 20%; temporarily set minimum replicas to 3 for high-traffic routes. Medium-term: Disable aggressive HPA scale-down while we roll out metric smoothing and alignment. Rolled out a Prometheus scrape frequency change for the request-per-second metric from 15s to 10s to reduce reporting lag.
action_items: Marco Nguyen - Align metric windows: update HPA custom metric to use the same 10s rolling window as KEDA queue scaler - due 2025-11-10
Priya Shah - Implement metric smoothing/EMA in metric adapter to reduce bounce from 5s spikes - due 2025-11-17
SRE Team - Add warm pool (pre-warmed pods) capability for model-serving pools with configurable warm size and health probe handshake - due 2025-12-05
Infra - Experiment with KEDA cooldown and polling intervals to reduce false positives - due 2025-11-24
Runtime - Add readiness gating improvements to minimize in-flight request failures during pod churn (graceful connection draining) - due 2025-12-01
Product - Document expected cold-start latency in public performance pages and include recommended min-replicas for latency-sensitive routes - due 2025-11-21
follow_ups: Create automated canary that simulates bursty traffic and validates no scale thrash under new configuration - owner: Performance CI - due 2025-11-30
Run cost/regressions analysis on increased min-replicas and warm pools to produce ROI tradeoffs - owner: Finance + Runtime - due 2025-12-08
Schedule cross-team review of autoscaler signals and thresholds (SRE, Runtime, Product) - owner: Aisha Patel - meeting by 2025-11-13
postmortem_notes: We confirmed that mixed signals between queue-length scalers and resource-based HPAs are a common source of thrashing when scraping/aggregation windows differ. KEDA performed appropriately for queue-driven surges but HPA reacted to ephemeral CPU drops during gaps in bursting. The cold-start penalty amplified user impact. Recommendation: prefer a primary scaling signal per workload (queue for bursty request patterns) and make secondary signals advisory, not mandatory. Also adopt warming strategies for model-serving workloads.
review_feedback: PM: Ensure product docs + runbooks are updated so customers can opt into higher min-replica tiers for SLO-critical routes (Sasha Lee)
Design: UX for Console scaling toggle should present cost vs latency tradeoffs before changing min-replicas (Diego Alvarez)
Security: Verify warm pool pre-warmed images do not introduce secret leakage from cached in-memory state (Marta Kovacs)
Eng Lead: Consider a single autoscaling controller that composes KEDA and HPA signals instead of policed override (Liam O'Connor)
resolution: Applied stabilization window increase and min-replica temporary floor. Rolled metric window alignment changes and smoothing in metric adapter. Planned warm pool and readiness gating work for next quarter. Monitoring added to detect scale thrash (defined as >3 scale events within 10 minutes).
status_notes: Marked Done after fixes merged and canary passed (2025-11-17). Remaining work scheduled as follow-ups in runtime-autoscaling-stability project.
notes_for_oncall: If alerts for rapid replica churn recur, immediately set affected deployment's HPA.minReplicas to 2 and notify Runtime on-call. Preserve logs and Grafana snapshots for the 30m window preceding the first scale event.
